**Wise refiles US bank charter application after OCC rejection**

*Wise is refiling its US trust bank charter application after the OCC cited anti-money-laundering and compliance deficiencies, complicating its planned listing move from London to New York.*

Wise is refiling its application for a US trust bank charter after the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) rejected its initial submission, citing anti-money-laundering and countering the financing of terrorism deficiencies alongside broader compliance concerns. Wise has acknowledged a consent order issued in July 2025 related to those issues but has not detailed what changes it is making to the resubmitted application.

The charter would give Wise direct access to US payment rails rather than relying on banking partners, a structural dependency that constrains margins and operational control. Wise announced in April that it planned to move its primary stock listing from London to the US, framing the shift as better alignment with its investor base and growth markets. A charter rejection on compliance grounds makes clear that US regulatory access is a harder problem to solve than a listing move.

Regulatory entry to the US remains a bottleneck for European fintechs even as capital markets access opens up. Wise's experience will be closely watched by peers weighing similar strategies.

*Sources: [Wise to refile US trust bank charter application after OCC rejection](https://thepaypers.com/fintech/news/wise-to-refile-us-trust-bank-charter-application-after-occ-rejection) — The Paypers*

**Lloyds, Barclays customers hit by UK online payments outage**

*A second major UK payments disruption in weeks raises fresh questions about the resilience of the country's payment infrastructure.*

Customers of several UK banks, such as Lloyds and Barclays, were unable to make online payments on Monday. The cause and duration of the disruption have not been publicly detailed.

The incident follows a Worldpay outage on June 23 that disrupted card payments across the UK during a World Cup match. Two significant outages within roughly a month are intensifying scrutiny of operational resilience across the UK payments stack, at a time when regulators and HM Treasury are consulting on the next generation of payments infrastructure. The Bank of England and the Payment Systems Regulator have both flagged concentration risk and single points of failure as areas of concern in recent assessments.

Merchants and billers exposed to repeated card and online payment failures face direct revenue losses, strengthening the commercial case for multi-rail payment strategies. Pay-by-bank and other alternative rails gain relevance not solely as cost-saving measures but as redundancy layers that reduce dependence on any single payment channel.

*Sources: [Outage leaves UK bank customers unable to make payments](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48151/outage-leaves-uk-bank-customers-unable-to-make-payments?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

stories.original:
**Monzo takes pension transfer speed campaign to Parliament**

*The digital bank is calling for a mandatory 30-day deadline on pension transfers, pushing open finance principles into retirement savings.*

Monzo is pressing Parliament to impose a 30-day maximum timeframe for pension transfers, arguing that current delays undermine consumer control over retirement savings. The campaign brings open finance advocacy directly into legislative debate at a time when the UK government has signalled broader ambitions for data-driven financial services.

Pension portability has long been a frustration for consumers and a test case for whether open finance can deliver practical benefits beyond payments and credit. Transfer times vary widely across providers, with some taking months. A mandatory deadline would force legacy pension administrators to modernise their processes, potentially opening the door to API-based data sharing that mirrors what open banking has achieved in current accounts.

Chancellor Rachel Reeves announced an open finance push focused on SME lending on July 14, 2025, and the Financial Conduct Authority's broader open finance roadmap targets 2030. Monzo says it sees pension reform as both a policy priority and a competitive opportunity, positioning itself as the destination for consolidated retirement savings.

*Sources: [Monzo Calls for 30-dayPension Transfer Deadline at Parliament](https://thefintechtimes.com/monzo-calls-for-30-daypension-transfer-deadline-at-parliament/) — The Fintech Times*
